history.method: unique `name:` declarations added in git history for tool source paths (lower bound)

tools.name: fs.list
tools.description: List a directory: names, sizes, dates. Use `kind` to get only executables or only folders.

tools.name: fs.read
tools.description: Read a file. Returns numbered lines (or a hex dump for binary files) plus entropy and a file hash when it is binary.

tools.name: fs.write
tools.description: Write a file (missing folders are created). Overwrites — for small edits use fs.patch.

tools.name: fs.patch
tools.description: Exact search/replace in a file. Simple, traceable, no fuzzy matching. Returns a diff.

tools.name: fs.search
tools.description: Regex search across files under a folder. Returns file:line:match. Use this before reading whole files.

tools.name: fs.grep
tools.description: Fast content search in ONE file (or every file under a folder) with context. Good for following flow in logs or source.

tools.name: fs.move
tools.description: Move or rename a file/folder. Creates the target folders.

tools.name: fs.copy
tools.description: Copy a file or folder (recursive).

tools.name: fs.delete
tools.description: Delete a file or folder. Moves to the recycle bin where possible (Win/mac), otherwise permanent. Always goes through the guard.

tools.name: fs.find
tools.description: Find files by name under a folder, recursively. Use this to locate a document you only know the name or extension of (e.g. a CV or an invoice) before reading it. Matches the file name, not the content

tools.name: fs.stat
tools.description: Metadata: size, dates, permissions, hash, entropy, file-type magic.

tools.name: fs.mkdir
tools.description: Create a folder (recursive).

tools.name: fs.tar
tools.description: Pack or unpack with the system tar (built into Windows 10+). Use it to move a folder around or extract an archive.

tools.name: shell.run
tools.description: Run a command and wait. Everything is allowed — the guard only stops what is irreversible or destructive. cwd defaults to the workspace.

tools.name: shell.bg
tools.description: Start a long-running job in the background and get an id. Use for servers, watchers, ghidra-headless, captures.

tools.name: shell.jobs
tools.description: List background jobs and their latest output. Use to follow servers and captures.

tools.name: shell.stop
tools.description: Stop a background job (SIGTERM, then SIGKILL).

tools.name: shell.env
tools.description: Read environment variables and shell settings. Useful before building commands.

tools.name: sys.info
tools.description: Machine status: OS, architecture, CPU, memory, home dir, workspace, node version.

tools.name: sys.ps
tools.description: Process list (name, pid, memory, cpu). Filterable with a regex.

tools.name: sys.ports
tools.description: Listening ports + pid. Use it to see what already runs (e.g. the MAJIN ui, frida, ollama).

tools.name: sys.fs_usage
tools.description: Disks and free space. Handy before unpacking something big.

tools.name: sys.procs_top
tools.description: Quick top-N by CPU/memory with the command line — used to spot suspicious processes.

tools.name: sys.services
tools.description: Services/processes that start automatically — persistence check (RE and plain debugging).

tools.name: net.dns
tools.description: Look up a domain (A/AAAA/TXT/CNAME/NS/MX). Used to follow IOCs found in a binary.

tools.name: net.tcp
tools.description: Probe a TCP port (open/closed) with a timeout. Only use it against things you own.

tools.name: net.http
tools.description: Raw HTTP request (method, headers, body). Use for your own APIs and for testing a local web service.

tools.name: net.serve
tools.description: Start a temporary HTTP server that shares a folder (to pull samples into the sandbox). Returns the URL + job id.

tools.name: net.serve_stop
tools.description: Stop a temporary sharing server.

tools.name: screen.capture
tools.description: Take a screenshot (PNG). On Windows via .NET; needs no extra software.

tools.name: screen.claim
tools.description: Read what is in the clipboard (text/file). Handy after the user selected something in a binary.

tools.name: sys.notify
tools.description: Push a Windows toast notification or let MAJIN speak out loud. Use it when a long job finishes.

tools.name: web.search
tools.description: Search the web. No API key needed (duckduckgo/bing fallback). Returns title, url and snippet.

tools.name: web.fetch
tools.description: Read a URL with GET/HEAD as clean text (or json/raw). For POST/PUT/DELETE or other external actions use approval-gated net.http. Follows redirects, size-capped.

tools.name: web.download
tools.description: Download a file into the workspace (samples, archives, documents). Executables require an approval — an agent should not run something by accident.

tools.name: browser.open
tools.description: Open or navigate a real browser page using Playwright Core. Uses an isolated persistent MAJIN profile. By default tools never submit forms. The owner host can authorize writes to exact origins; a mode

tools.name: browser.read
tools.description: Read visible text from the page (or one selector) — the actual words on the page, capped.

tools.name: browser.click
tools.description: Click one page element selected by a Playwright CSS/text selector or by a Set-of-Marks ref from browser.inspect marks=true. Pass frame (iframe selector from browser.inspect) when the element lives ins

tools.name: browser.form
tools.description: Observe current form fields by live accessible labels/types, dropdown options, required/native validation, alert errors and submit/next buttons. Values stay hidden. Use before browser.form_fill and af

tools.name: browser.form_fill
tools.description: Set 1–12 previously observed form fields in order using exact labels or f-refs as keys in values. Text/select values are strings; checkboxes use true/false; file fields use workspace file paths. Reobs

tools.name: browser.form_submit
tools.description: Click ONE previously observed next/review/submit button by its exact label or f-ref. Regrounds changed DOM, never automatically repeats submission. Returns current form, native/server errors and visib

tools.name: browser.fill
tools.description: Fill a text, email, number, date or textarea control by selector. Pass frame (iframe selector from browser.inspect) when the control lives inside an iframe. Values are not written to the action log. D

tools.name: browser.shot
tools.description: Capture a PNG screenshot of the current page into the workspace (default shots/shot-<time>.png). ifChanged=true reuses the previous file when the pixels are identical. The saved PNG is real visual evi

tools.name: browser.upload
tools.description: Attach a local file to a file input. This only selects the file in the browser; it is not uploaded until the user submits, and submission is blocked.

tools.name: browser.verify
tools.description: Verify a REAL post-action browser outcome on the current page: live URL (fragment, exact path, exact origin), title, unique visible element, element text, checkbox state, enabled state, or exact match

tools.name: browser.elements
tools.description: W6 Set-of-Marks grounding: number every interactive element on the open page, draw the matching pink marks on screen, and return the references so browser.click({ref:"eN"}) hits deterministically inst

tools.name: browser.clear_marks
tools.description: Remove MAJIN Set-of-Marks overlays and data-majin-ref attributes from the current page (or from one iframe via frame) and forget the cached refs. This changes only MAJIN annotations; it does not alter

tools.name: browser.close
tools.description: Close the current Playwright browser session. The isolated persistent profile is kept for next time.

tools.name: media.generate_image
tools.description: Generate one image using an OpenAI-compatible provider and save it in the workspace. Requires a configured provider/model that supports /images/generations; remote generation may cost money.

tools.name: media.speak
tools.description: Synthesize spoken audio from text with an OpenAI-compatible /audio/speech provider and save it locally. Requires a configured speech model; remote generation may cost money.

tools.name: re.analyze
tools.description: Full triage of a binary: format, headers, sections+entropy, imports/exports, packers, YARA, IOC strings, opcode patterns, a risk score and suggested next steps. Start here.

tools.name: re.strings
tools.description: Extract strings (ascii + utf16) with offsets. Filter with a regex. Used to find URLs, paths, mutexes and important API names.

tools.name: re.hexdump
tools.description: Hex dump at an offset. Used for headers, the overlay, packer signatures and raw comparison.

tools.name: re.search
tools.description: Pattern hunt in bytes: "4d 5a ?? (e8|eb)" or a text string. Returns offset + context.

tools.name: re.entropy
tools.description: Entropy profile per section + block. High entropy = packed or encrypted. Used to decide what to unpack.

tools.name: re.sections
tools.description: Section table with flags, entropy and deviation (name/size/perm). The deviations are what to look at.

tools.name: re.imports
tools.description: Import tables (DLL → functions) with risk flags. Delay imports included.

tools.name: re.exports
tools.description: Export table (for DLLs) + forwarded exports. Used to list hook and backend functions.

tools.name: re.yara
tools.description: Run YARA rules with the built-in mini engine — no yara binary needed. Add your own rules in rules/majin.yar.

tools.name: re.iocs
tools.description: Pull out and group IOCs (URLs, IPs, file paths, registry keys, mutexes, e-mail, GUIDs) and resolve domains when asked.

tools.name: re.overlay
tools.description: Read (and optionally extract) the data after the last section — where packers and self-extractors hide.

tools.name: re.extract
tools.description: Extract ZIP/APK/asar entries or a PE resource into the workspace. Used to reach embedded content.

tools.name: re.apk
tools.description: Android package: permissions, components, DEX sizes, signer — no apktool needed.

tools.name: re.pcap
tools.description: Summarize a pcap/pcapng: hosts, ports, HTTP requests and DNS names. Used for C2 traffic from a sandbox run.

tools.name: re.diff
tools.description: Compare two binaries (versions, variants, clean vs injected). Gives hash/import/string deltas plus a section diff.

tools.name: re.modules
tools.description: Modules/DLLs loaded in a running process + unusual paths. Used to see injection or hooking live.

tools.name: re.tool
tools.description: Hook up external RE tools when you need real power: ghidra (decompile), rizin, objdump, binwalk, upx, yara, jadx, apktool, ilspycmd. Auto-detects what is installed.

tools.name: re.tools
tools.description: Which external RE tools exist and what is missing. The built-in parser needs nothing — this is for deeper work.

tools.name: re.disasm
tools.description: Disassemble at an address/offset. Uses rizin/objdump when present — otherwise bytes + pattern analysis, never guesses.

tools.name: re.unpack
tools.description: Try to unpack known packers. UPX works directly; otherwise: entropy/section assessment + carving the overlay.

tools.name: re.hash
tools.description: MD5/SHA1/SHA256 + imphash for one or more files. Used to look up known samples.

tools.name: re.spec
tools.description: Turn a finished investigation into SPEC.md: observable behaviour, inputs/outputs, formats, error handling and open questions — every claim carrying the file offset it came from, and everything not pro

tools.name: re.rules
tools.description: List and save YARA rules in <home>/rules/majin.yar (MAJIN's own rule database).

tools.name: majin.configure
tools.description: Change MAJIN own configuration (routes, moa, providers, channels, guard, agent, tools, ui, budget, persona). A validated JSON patch; an invalid patch is rejected with a reason. Use intent for natural

tools.name: majin.routes
tools.description: Model routing: show, set or test the jobs (chat, tasks, tools, code, re, research, plan, analysis, final, summarize, aggregator, router, vision).

tools.name: majin.provider
tools.description: Manage providers: list | add | remove | test | models (list available models from /models).

tools.name: majin.moa
tools.description: Mixture-of-Agents: show | on | off | hard (only hard jobs) | set (references/aggregator/width). On by default.

tools.name: majin.guard
tools.description: The safety glass: status | mode(confirm|strict|off) | allow(tool) | disallow. The agent can NOT approve its own dangerous actions — a human always does that.

tools.name: majin.memory
tools.description: Long-term memory: remember(text) | recall(query) | forget(query) | list | clear. The agent stores preferences, projects and solutions here.

tools.name: majin.skill
tools.description: Learned skills (markdown in data/skills): list | save | read | delete | match. A skill is how a kind of task is done, step by step.

tools.name: majin.schedule
tools.description: Scheduled work: add | list | remove | run | pause | resume. Requests like "every morning 07:30: do X and send it to telegram" belong here.

tools.name: majin.channel
tools.description: Channels: status | telegram | whatsapp | send | pair. Sets bot keys, links devices and sends messages.

tools.name: majin.status
tools.description: Full status: config, routes, MOA, channels, external RE tools, budget, memory, skills, jobs, log path. Use it when the user asks "how are you doing?".

tools.name: majin.doctor
tools.description: Health check, human style: every capability gets OK / why-not / how-to-fix. Use it when something feels off, before the user asks you to guess. No network calls — it reads config and reports, then poi

tools.name: majin.selftest
tools.description: Diagnostics: provider keys, one real minimal call per provider, the tool registry, an RE check on its own binary, channel status, port, writability. Run this when something behaves oddly.

tools.name: majin.tools
tools.description: List every tool with its description and risk level. All of them are always on — there is no off switch.

tools.name: majin.backup
tools.description: Export/import everything MAJIN knows (config, memory, skills, schedules) as a tar.gz in workspace/backups.

tools.name: majin.ui
tools.description: Open the UI: on Windows a dedicated Edge/Chrome app window. action=open | theme | voice.

tools.name: majin.control
tools.description: Control the agent itself: restart | stop | pause | resume | clear (session) | sessions | history.

tools.name: majin.dataset
tools.description: Local trajectory recording used to make MAJIN better. OFF by default, redacted on write, stored next to the config, and never uploaded — exporting is a deliberate command you run.

tools.name: majin.adapter
tools.description: Safe external adapters (Del 7B): validate | create | list | remove. An adapter is a DECLARATIVE http-json descriptor (no code, https only, permission class read | external-write | external-post); an i

tools.name: majin.plugin
tools.description: Create, list, reload or remove custom MAJIN tools. A created JavaScript plugin runs with MAJIN process privileges, is hash-checked at startup and every invocation requires exec approval in normal guar

tools.name: agent.plan
tools.description: Write and update the visible work list for the session. Use it for more than 3 steps; the UI shows it live.

tools.name: agent.delegate
tools.description: Send a sub-problem to a subagent with its own step budget (it sees your tools but not your history). Use it for parallel digging — e.g. "analyse these 3 files".

tools.name: agent.moa
tools.description: Run an extra Mixture-of-Agents round on a sub-problem (several models in parallel + an aggregator). Use for hard decisions, not for everything.

tools.name: agent.approve
tools.description: Answer a pending confirmation in the UI (approve/deny). Only when the user explicitly told you to.
